description: Resolve a runtime stack trace against the project graph: paste the trace text in `trace` and get, per frame, which definitions in THIS project the frame's identifier names. The verb for "my service threw this in production, what code is that". Returns `kind: "trace-error"` with retained frames in input order, each carrying an `origin` (`in_project`, `node_modules`, `out_of_corpus`) and a `resolution` (`resolved`, `ambiguous`, `not_found`, `not_attempted`), plus `candidates[]` naming the file, symbol, member and declaration line. It is built to refuse overclaiming: a frame matching several definitions is `ambiguous`, with bounded candidates and `candidates_omitted` instead of a preferred match, a frame the graph was never asked about is `not_attempted` rather than a softer `not_found`, and `line_mismatch` marks a resolved frame whose own line sits at a different declaration, so a name-only match is visible instead of implied. `counts` closes over the reported frames and publishes `frames_omitted` and `unparsed_lines`, so a capped or unreadable input cannot look complete. No source maps are read: a frame inside built output says so instead of being rebound through a map that may be stale, so give it a trace from unbundled source or the source paths a map already resolved. The RESOLUTION outcome never fails the call: a trace in which nothing resolves is an ANSWER, and exits 0. A refused input still is a refusal: an empty or oversized `trace` returns `isError` with `FALLOW_INVALID_TRACE_OPTIONS`.

allow_remote_extends.description:
Allow trusted HTTPS config `extends` for this request. Defaults to false
and never grants process-global trust.

config.description: Path to a fallow config file.

production.description:
Production mode: exclude test, story, and dev files, only start/build
scripts, and report type-only dependencies.

root.description: Project root; defaults to the working directory.

source.description: Where the trace came from, echoed back as the payload's `source`.

threads.description: Parser thread count; defaults to CPU cores.

trace.description: The runtime stack trace text, pasted verbatim.

workspace.description: Workspace packages to analyze: name or repo-relative path, comma-separated list, globs, `!` negation.

name: trace_error
